history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration conduct an analysis to better understand how to calculate catalytic effects and anticipate where they should be realized throughout the implementation of projects, and that it take measures to increase funding entrusted to local civil society and community organizations directly to improve national capacity.
history.administration_response: In 2023, the Peacebuilding Fund commissioned an independent assignment to develop catalytic effect guidelines for the Fund. The document was finalized in March 2024. According to the findings, the interest of most stakeholders is in the non-financial catalytic effects of peacebuilding projects and is best measured at the country/project level. In 2023, to measure the amount that civil society organizations received from the Fund, the amount of financing received by national and local non-governmental organizations on an annual basis was calculated. While data for 2023 is not yet consolidated, in 2022, 25 per cent of Fund expenditures went to national or local civil society organizations. The Fund has taken measures to increase the funding entrusted to local civil society. Between 2021, 2022 and 2023 the share of the allocation of total approvals to national and local civil society organizations as direct recipients of funds was 0.8 per cent, 2.6 per cent and 3.9 per cent respectively. Over the three years, the number of national and local civil society organizations that were direct recipients of funds from the Peacebuilding Fund increased from 2 to 5 to 11. The Administration therefore requests closure of this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that the catalytic effects have now been well calculated and analysed, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
